messages:
marty-customer: Hi team — our latest invoice INV-2026-9876 shows NY sales tax line (8.875%) even though the billed entity is 'Acme EU LTD' (registered in NJ for US ops), we don't have nexus in NY. Can you check?
alyssa-support: sorry about that, tagging @jamal-billing and @sophie-finance. Do you have a screenshot or the raw invoice pdf?
marty-customer: attaching screenshot (see line item). Also it looks like the tax was applied only to the proration charge when they upgraded mid-cycle: looks like the proration used the account parent mailing addr (NY HQ) not the billed legal entity.
jamal-billing: digging in — invoice ID INV-2026-9876, account_acct=acct_73f, charge lines:
```
- subscription: monthly-basic (proration) $120.00
- prorated period: 2026-02-10 to 2026-03-01
- tax (NY): $10.65
```
jamal-billing: system shows tax jurisdiction resolved from billing_profile.address.city = New York, NY. That's unexpected, user-provided billing_profile.entity_id suggests NJ.
sophie-finance: possible cause: when a child entity upgrades via hosted checkout, we merge payment info from parent for card capture but should compute tax based on entity-level tax_profile. If merge order reversed, tax jurisdiction could come from parent mailing addr.
alyssa-support: @marty-customer quick question — did you complete checkout via the 'Switch plan' in-app flow or via invoice/hosted link?
marty-customer: In-app 'Switch plan' from the org admin UI. We have two internal orgs under same account: "Acme US (NY HQ)" and "Acme EU LTD (NJ)". We picked the EU LTD billing entity in the UI.
jamal-billing: I'm seeing a race where payment_method.attach() completes before tax_profile.resolve(), so the invoice_builder cached the parent_profile for proration lines. I'll open a bug. For immediate fix we can: 1) issue a corrected invoice with tax removed for the proration line, 2) refund the tax portion / credit note, and 3) re-run tax calc pipeline to avoid double charging.
sophie-finance: agree. I'll prepare a credit note. @jamal-billing can you confirm the tax_exempt flag and provide the corrected net/total so finance can apply a credit?
jamal-billing: corrected numbers: net $120.00, tax 0.00 (should be 0), total $120.00. Tax charged was $10.65. Refund amount = $10.65. Will create internal ticket TB-7892 and add logs.
alyssa-support: @marty-customer we'll process the credit and send a new invoice PDF within 24 hours. Also: did the payment for the invoice succeed? I see two payment attempts and one decline. Any card issues on your side?
marty-customer: We saw a decline on first try (3D Secure pop-up failed), second attempt succeeded but was delayed — can you confirm we won't be double-charged after the credit?
jamal-billing: Payment log snippet:
```
- attempt 1: pm_card-visa: status=requires_action -> 3ds failed -> declined
- attempt 2: pm_card-visa: status=succeeded -> captured $130.65 (includes tax)
```
jamal-billing: We'll issue a refund for $10.65 to the same payment method; capture id cap_44y. Refund will be tied to INV-2026-9876 and appear on bank statements as 'Redwood Refund'.
sophie-finance: creating credit note CN-2026-452 and refund PR-330. ETA 1-3 business days for bank to reflect.
alyssa-support: internal follow-ups: ticket TB-7892 (fix tax_profile race), KB draft to advise customers about multi-entity upgrades and proration tax handling, and outreach to eng to add a regression test.
jamal-billing: engineer notes for the ticket: ensure invoice_builder binds tax_profile from chosen_billing_entity before attaching payment_method; add test for in-app plan switch with multiple entities.
invoice-bot: Payment refund created: PR-330, Credit note CN-2026-452; Refund status: pending -> will update thread when settled. :white_check_mark:
alyssa-support: @marty-customer once refund completes I'll DM you the refund receipt and updated invoice. Really sorry for the confusion — we'll waive any fees and follow up if anything else crops up. :heart:
marty-customer: thanks, appreciate the quick triage — will keep an eye out for the receipt.
